business.name: Review Engine
business.offer_line: Your customers are happy and your Google listing does not show it. A steady flow of new reviews every month, without anyone in your business having to ask for one.

brand.logo: none supplied — the site draws its own monogram

kit.name: Waitlist Green
kit.best_for: Prelaunch funnels — one page, one question
kit.voice: One promise, one ask, no filler. It is honest that the thing does not exist yet and specific about what joining gets you.
kit.usage: Green appears exactly once per page: the join button. A second green element on a waitlist page costs signups.

archetype.label: Prelaunch validation funnel
archetype.voice: Direct and unembarrassed. It is asking for a small commitment to an idea that does not exist yet, so it must be specific about what it is, honest that it is early, and clear about what happens next. No fake scarcity.
archetype.summary: One page that turns an idea into evidence. It states the promise, asks for a name and an email, and counts. Nothing else is built until enough people say they want it.

items.title: An automatic post-job review request by SMS or email, with a one-tap link
QR cards for the counter, the van and the invoice

items.body: You are early. Nothing is built yet, and that is the point: the people on this list decide what gets built.

items.title: Next — the first version, for this list only
items.body: Everyone here sees it before anyone else, and pays less than everyone else, permanently.

items.title: Then — open to everyone
items.body: At full price, with the list's fingerprints all over it.

sections.title: Join the waitlist
sections.body: A name and an email. No spam, no drip sequence — you hear from us when there is something real to see.

sections.title: Want it to exist?
sections.body: That is the whole ask. A name on the list is the signal that decides whether this gets built.

pages.title: What happens next
pages.purpose: Answer the suspicion that a waitlist is a trick.

hero.title: What happens next
hero.lede: What joining actually means, and what it does not.

items.q: Is this real, or an idea?
items.a: An idea, openly. It gets built if enough people here say they want it. That is what the list is for.

items.q: Am I committing to buy anything?
items.a: No. You are saying you would be interested. Nothing is charged, and there is nothing to charge for yet.

items.q: What do you do with my email?
items.a: Write to you when there is something to see. It is not sold, shared, or added to anything else.

items.q: What if it never gets built?
items.a: Then you get one message saying so. That is a real outcome and you deserve to be told.

sections.title: Still in?
sections.body: Add your name and we will keep you posted either way.
